(Per Hon'ble Sri Justice K. Lakshman) Heard Sri P.Raghuvaran, learned counsel appearing for the appellant and Sri T.Sudhakar Reddy, learned counsel for the respondent.

2. Feeling aggrieved and dissatisfied by the order and decree dated 12.03.2018 in O.P.No.426 of 2009 passed by learned XVI Additional District and Sessions Judge-cum-XVI Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge-cum-III Additional Family Court, Ranga Reddy District at Malkajgiri.
Appellant/wife preferred the present appeal.

sentences.text: The respondent/husband filed aforesaid O.P against the appellant/wife seeking dissolution of marriage on the ground of cruelty as well as desertion contending as follows:
i. The marriage of the respondent with the appellant was performed on 24.04.2006.
According to him, he picked up the name of the appellant from the list of brides maintained by Sweet Home Marriage Bureau, Chikkadpally, Hyderabad.

In the 2nd week of March 2006, the appellant and her younger sister conversed with the respondent in the said marriage bureau itself and invited the respondent to the house of their maternal uncle, Mr M.Venkateswarlu, situated at Yousufguda, Hyderabad,
where detailed discussions were held for settlement of the marriage.
Accordingly, the respondent and his parents visited the house of the maternal uncle of the appellant as programmed.
The mother and younger sister of the appellant were present.
Her brother and father were not present.
On enquiry, she informed the respondent that her father was sick at Madhya Pradesh Forest and getting Herbal Juice treatment and her brother was pre-occupied in the coal mines at Madhya Pradesh.
He has believed the said version of the appellant bonafidely.
Except the bio-data, he has not verified the antecedents and family history of the appellant.
ii. The engagement was fixed on 24.03.2006.
At the time of engagement, the respondent parents expressed doubt with regard to the unilateral decision of the appellant with regard to her marriage.
However, the respondent was to leave USA, therefore he has accepted the said engagement.
Accordingly, the betrothal function was held on 24.03.2006 at Taj Mahal Hotel, Abids, Hyderabad.

Thereafter, marriage was fixed on 24.04.2006 as C. Lajvanthi vs C. Muralikrishna Rao on 7 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31475069/

sentences.text: The said marriage was consummated on 24.04.2006 itself.
Thereafter, reception was held on 26.04.2006.
The brother of appellant, her seven maternal aunts (mother's sisters) were absent.
He has presented gold jewellery like Ruby Necklace, Pustela Tadu and Gundla Chain etc., weighing 15 tolas and also presented pattu sarees worth 3 to 4 lakhs.

They went to Tirupati on 12.05.2006 and thereafter the appellant joined his company on 17.05.2006.
iii.
She started picking up quarrels with his parents on trivial issues with loud voice.
His parents were shocked and surprised at the queer behaviour and the defiant attitude of the appellant herein.
She also exhibited quarrelsome and rebellious attitude towards the respondent and his parents.
She used to misbehave with him on petty issues.
Even then, his father went to Warangal on 19.05.2006 and brought her father.
They have discussed with regard to the said attitude of the appellant.
Even then there was no change in her attitude.
Discussions were held in the presence of father of the appellant and maternal uncle, retired teacher of the appellant.
4. According to respondent, he and the appellant lead conjugal life from 17.05.2006 to 08.06.2006.

Thereafter, appellant expressed some ill- health and when he got her examined on 08.06.2006 and medical check- up in M/s.Vijayalaxmi Nursing Home at Narayanaguda, Hyderabad and doctors informed her that she was pregnant.
i.
She went to her mother's house on 08.06.2006 in the month of Ashada Masam.
She never came back.
ii. While going, she took all her gold ornaments and pattu sarees etc., presented by the respondent.
She never returned to her matrimonial house.
iii. During her stay with the respondent, she never treated her husband with affection and respect.
iv. She ill-treated her in-laws.
She insulted and humiliated them.
v. Whenever she needed medical check-up and medicines, she used to call respondent over phone.
He used to attend the same.
vi. On 10.07.2006, she requested the respondent not to come to her mother's house thereafter.
In spite of it, he got treated the appellant in Fernandez Hospital, Hyderabad from 12.06.2006 upto 20.12.2006.
He has also paid all medical expensed incurred.
Thereafter, there was no communication to him from the appellant.

It is further contended that, suddenly on 29.01.2007 at 9 a.m., he received a telephonic message informing him that she blessed with a son and the delivery of the appellant took place in Sashi Hospital, Dilsukhnagar, Hyderabad.
He could not identify the tone of the caller.
Thereafter, he rushed to the said Nursing Home and saw the new born baby and gave Rs.5,000/- to the appellant.
vii. He could not stay there for a long time due to the insulting behaviour of the appellant.
On 19th day of delivery i.e. 16.02.2007, the appellant fixed Barasala function and informed the same to the respondent without inviting his parents.
Even then they have attended the said function.

sentences.text: In the month of December, 2007, the respondent went to the appellant's mother house, after waiting for a long period of 18 months and requested her to join his company.
She bluntly refused the same.
ix. She insisted the respondent to setup a separate family abandoning his old and handicapped father and mother.
His mother was suffering with cancer.
x. Thus, according to the respondent/husband, the appellant subjected him to cruelty and deserted him.
5. The appellant filed counter denying the said allegations.
According to her, she never subjected him to cruelty.
She has created all the said allegations only to file the present application and get rid of her.
i. She came from a respectable and traditional family and her father and mother brought her up with utmost love and affection.
ii. Her father is a retired Government Employee, who was a Junior Assistant in a Regional Transport Office.
He was getting pension.
Her brother is an ex-serviceman working with Coal India Limited.
Therefore, the allegations made by the respondent that her father and brother did not attend the engagement, reception, etc., with some intension of false and baseless.
iii. During her stay in the matrimonial house, the respondent and his parents discontinued the maid servant and started using her as a maid servant.
She was helpless and was subjected to humiliation.
She used to work from 5 a.m. to 11 p.m.
They used to abuse and harass her for small things.
iv. His sister used to beat her for no fault of her.
v. She was blessed with a male baby on 29.01.2007 after a cesarean operation.
vi. The respondent came to the said hospital on 5th day of her delivery and informed her that he will take care of her son's welfare.
Cradle ceremony was arranged on 23.04.2007 by booking a Hotel at Hotel Shivani situated at Dilsukhnagar.
vii. On 17.04.2007, her parents invited her in-laws and requested them to attend the said ceremony to bless the child.
Even then, they have abused her parents in filthy language.
viii. She stayed at her in-laws house from 24.04.2006 to 21.09.2006 and after that the respondent/husband used to visit her mother's place very often.
ix. He got a saree for her on 28.01.2007.
Next day after the delivery, his mother, his sister and her husband, their children and relatives came to the hospital to wish the child.
x. On 16.02.2007, they have conducted cradle ceremony.
Thus, she never subjected the respondent with cruelty and never deserted him.
xi. Even then she has received a notice in the aforesaid O.P. on 16.08.2008.
The respondent is in the clutches of his parents and they were habituated to western culture and they were unable to C. Lajvanthi vs C. Muralikrishna Rao on 7 June, 2024

They used to harass her.
xiii. He used to work in U.S.A and used to get 600 dollars per month.

He stayed there for about 8 years and earned Rs.2 crores.
xv. Her husband is NRI and he went to USA on L1 Visa.
He returned to India as green card holder.

With the said contentions, she sought to dismiss the aforesaid O.P.
filed by respondent/husband and she has also filed a petition under Section 9 of Hindu Marriage Act vide O.P.No.427 of 2009 against the respondent/husband seeking restitution of conjugal rights.
6. To prove the said claim, the respondent/husband examined himself as PW1 and marked Exs.P1 to P51 documents.

To disprove the said allegations, her claim of restitution of conjugal rights,
appellant/wife examined herself as RW1 and filed Exs.R1 to R17 documents.
7.

On consideration of the entire evidence, the learned Family Court vide impugned order dated 12.03.2018 allowed the application filed by the husband/respondent seeking dissolution of the marriage by dissolving their marriage by way of granting decree of divorce.
The learned Family Court dismissed the O.P. filed by appellant/wife seeking restitution of conjugal rights.
The appellant/wife preferred the present appeal feeling aggrieved by the Order in O.P.No.426 of 2009 i.e., granting decree of divorce.
She did not file any appeal challenging the said Order dismissing the O.P. filed by her i.e., O.P.No.427 of 2009 seeking restitution of conjugal rights.
Therefore, the said Order attained finality.
Challenging the said order, she filed an appeal.

This Court granted interim stay on 10.04.2018.
8.
The aforesaid facts would reveal that there is no dispute with regard to the marriage of the parties on 24.04.2006, and reception on 26.04.2006.

It is also not in dispute that the appellant herein has filed a petition vide D.V.C.No.1 of 2009 against the respondent/husband under Section 9(b) and Section 37(2)(c) of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 seeking certain reliefs.

entities.text: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Vide Order dated 01.10.2010, Learned Magistrate allowed the said DVC directing the respondent, his father to pay an amount of Rs.2,000/- per month or provide alternative accommodation.
Learned magistrate also directed the respondent to return an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- to the appellant with regard to the marriage expenditure and Rs.10,000/- towards medical expenses.

The Magistrate further directed the respondent to pay an amount of Rs.9,000/-
per month towards the maintenance of the appellant and her son from the date of the said Order.
9. According to Sri T. Sudharkar Reddy, learned counsel, respondent has preferred an appeal against the said Order and the same was allowed.

It is also not in dispute that at the instance of the appellant, C.C.No.163 of 2009 was registered against the respondent, his father, mother and sister for the offences under Section 498A of IPC, r/w 34 of IPC and Section 4 and 6 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.
The same ended in acquittal vide Judgment dated 29.01.2018.

sentences.text: It is relevant to note that the appellant herein preferred an appeal against the said judgment vide Crl.A.No.267 of 2018 and the same was dismissed.

According to T.Sudhakar Reddy, learned counsel for the respondent, implicating the respondent/husband and his family members in Criminal case for the offence under Section 498A of IPC, the same ended in acquittal and the same was not challenged by the appellant and therefore amounts to cruelty.

11. It is also not in dispute that the appellant and her son have filed a suit by O.S.No.635 of 2016 against respondent seeking partition and separate possession of suit schedule properties and the same is pending.
The respondent has filed petition under Order 7 Rule 11 of CPC to reject the plaint and the same was dismissed.
Challenging the said Order, the respondent has filed a revision and the same was also dismissed.
However, the said suit is pending.
12. The appellant has filed an application under Section 125 of Cr.P.C contending that the respondent failed to pay the amount awarded by the learned Magistrate in D.V.C.No.1 of 2009.
The said application was allowed and he was sent to jail for one month.

13. The following cases were filed, pending and disposed between the parties:
a. C.C.No.163 of 2009 filed against the respondent and his parents for the offences under Section 498A of IPC, r/w 34 of IPC under Section 4 and 6 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 and the same was ended in acquittal.
b. D.V.C.No.1 of 2009 filed by her and the same was allowed.
The respondent has filed an appeal and the same was allowed.
c. The respondent has filed O.P.No.426 of 2009 seeking dissolution of marriage and the same was allowed.
d. The appellant has filed a petition in O.P.No.427 of 2009 seeking restitution of conjugal rights and the same was dismissed.
e. Crl.A.No.703 of 2010 filed by the appellant was dismissed.
f. Vide Order dated 07.05.2010 in Crl.M.P.No.1059 of 2009 in D.V.C.No.1 of 2009, respondent was sent to prison for a period of one month.
g. Vide Order dated 02.11.2010 in Crl.M.P.No.2131 of 2010 in Crl.M.P.No.598 of 2009 in D.V.C.No.1 of 2009, the respondent was sent to prison for a period of one month.
h. She has also filed Crl.M.P.No.30 of 2017 in D.V.C.No.1 of 2009 against the respondent.
i. A suit vide O.S.No.635 of 2016 filed by the appellant against the respondent seeking partition of the suit schedule property is also pending.
j. The appellant/wife preferred an appeal vide Crl.A.No.267 of 2018 challenging the judgment dated 29.01.2018 and the same was also dismissed.

sentences.text: She has filed a petition under Section 125 of Cr.P.C in M.C.No.112 of 2019 and the same is pending.
l. The present appeal i.e., F.C.A.No.134 of 2018.
14. The aforesaid facts would reveal that there is a strained relationship between the respondent and the appellant.

On consideration of entire evidence, vide impugned order, learned Family Court allowed the O.P. filed by respondent/husband and granted decree of divorce dissolving the marriage of the parties dated 24.04.2006.
There is no error in it.
They are staying separately since almost 18 years.
15. During cross examination, appellant (RW.1) categorically admitted that she is residing with her in-laws and her husband did not live together after marriage.
She came to know that the house belongs to her mother-in-law and it is an ancestral property.
She filed suit of partition against the said house.
Ex.P51 is the certificate copy of the plaint in O.S.No.635 of 2016.
After filing of the divorce application by her husband, she filed O.P.No.427 of 2009 seeking restitution of conjugal rights.
She has also admitted about lodging the complaint against the respondent and his parents vide C.C.No.163 of 2009 and filing of D.V.C.No.1 of 2009.
In the said petition, she has mentioned that she was necked out from the house in the month of July 2006 finally.
16. From 28.07.2008 onwards, she and her husband are living separately without any matrimonial relationship.
The respondent/husband used to reside in the house of his mother at the time of her marriage, her father-in-law was 60 years old and he was a handicapped person.
The respondent came to India two (02) weeks before the marriage.
After the marriage, the respondent stayed in India.
She has not filed any documents to show that she has paid dowry amount.
Before the marriage, negotiations took place in the house of Mr. M.Venkateswarlu, her maternal uncle.
17. She also admitted that filing appeal against order in D.V.C.No.1 of 2009 seeking enhancement.
Her mother-in-law and husband took her to Maternity Nursing Home, Narayanguda on 08.06.2006 and on that day, her pregnancy was confirmed.
She took treatment in Shashi Nursing Home while she was on pregnancy up to December 2006.
Her husband and parents spent on the medical expenses.
While pregnant, she underwent operation with the support of the her mother.
She gave birth to a son on 29.01.2007.
Her husband presented a saree to the appellant/wife after the delivery as per the custom.
Her sister-in-law and mother-in-law came to the hospital to visit her.

The family of the respondent came to the function performed by them in their house on 16.02.2007.
18.
She also admitted that after marriage, they went to Tirupati.
From 29.01.2006, she was residing with her parents and the respondent was residing with his parents.
Her in-laws and husband are living in one house.
His elder brother is residing in U.S.A.
The respondent is looking after his parents.
She came to know that her mother-in-law was suffering with cancer.
They had no sexual relationship up to 20.07.2008.
Except one boy child, she has no other children.
The respondent is paying an amount of Rs.8,000/- per month regularly.

sentences.text: The aforesaid facts would reveal that the relationship between the appellant and the respondent is strained because of the filing of cases.
He was sent to jail twice for not implementing the order in D.V.C.No.1 of 2009.
She has lodged a complaint against the respondent/husband, his parents and his brother for the offence under Section 498-A of I.P.C and the same ended in acquittal.
No appeal was preferred.
20. It is not in dispute that respondent father was a handicapped person, retired Government employee, his mother is suffering with cancer, her brother is residing in U.S.A.
Even the respondent came from U.S.A. after staying there for some time.
She has filed a suit vide O.S.No.635 of 2016 seeking partition of the suit schedule property despite knowing that the said property is an ancestral property of her mother-in-law.
She has also filed a case under Section 125 of Cr.P.C and M.C.No.112 of 2019.
However, they are having one son born on 29.01.2007.
The appellant is an advocate.
The respondent is claiming that he is not doing anything now.
According to the appellant, he is doing business and have earned money over properties.
21. The aforesaid facts would reveal that they are staying separately from 20.07.2008 without having a conjugal life between them.
Thus, the marriage of appellant with the respondent was irretrievably brokedown.
However, it is not a ground to grant divorce by the Family Court or by this Court.
However, the same can be considered as an aspect to come to a conclusion with regard to cruelty.
While deciding the matrimonial disputes, we have to consider the social aspects.

The said principle was also laid by a full bench of this Court in the case of Panati Madhusudhana Reddy Vs.
Maddali Renuka @ Suhasini1.
22.

Maddali Renuka @ Suhasini1

sentences.text: In the light of the aforesaid discussion, we are of the considered view that learned Family Court has rightly dissolved the marriage of the appellant and the respondent.
It is a reasoned order and well founded.
As discussed supra, according to the appellant (RW.1), respondent/husband declined to pay Rs.8,000/- per month to her and her son towards maintenance.
The aforesaid suit filed by the appellant seeking partition, is pending.
There is no dispute that the appellant and respondent have been blessed with a male child on 29.01.2007.
The said fact is not disputed by the respondent/husband also.
The boy is 17 years old now and he is with the appellant.
24. In the light of the aforesaid discussion, this Court is of the considered view that the appellant is entitled for an amount of Rs.10,00,000/- (Rupees Ten Lakhs Only) towards permanent alimony.
The said amount is towards full and final settlement in D.V.C.No.1 of 2009 including all her claims in D.V.C.No.1 of 2009 and M.C.No.112 of 2019.

The respondent shall pay this amount to the appellant within two (02) months from the date of receipt of copy of this Order, failing which liberty is granted to wife to take steps in accordance with law.
The respondent is at liberty to place reliance on this Order in the said suit i.e., O.S.No.635 of 2016 filed by the appellant seeking partition.
25. With the aforesaid directions, this appeal is disposed of.
There shall be no order as to costs.
26. As a sequel, miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending shall stand closed.
